title: Valerian bath for bedtime tension
subtitle: A warming herbal bath for physical tension before bed
excerpt: Fifty grams of dried valerian root steeped in one litre of water, strained, and poured into a bath. Traditionally prepared to ease physical tension in the body before sleep. A 15-20 minute soak taken 30-60 minutes before bed.
sourceNotes: Maud Grieve, A Modern Herbal (1931), Valeriana officinalis entry : external preparations and bath use. EMA HMPC Community herbal monograph on Valeriana officinalis L., radix (2006, updated 2016) .  preparation guidance and safety review.

recipe.makeAheadNotes: Dried valerian root stores up to 12 months in a sealed tin away from light. Prepare fresh each time.

glossaryTerms.definition: A preparation where a strong infusion or decoction of dried herb is strained and added to a full bath for external absorption through the skin.

content.text: made by steeping 50 g of dried valerian root in one litre of water for 20 minutes, straining, and adding the liquid to a warm bath. Traditionally prepared to ease physical tension held in the muscles before sleep. The smell is strong and earthy: be prepared for it. The root has a pronounced, pungent scent that some find very effective and others find challenging. Soak for 15-20 minutes.

attrs.title: Precautions
attrs.body:
Not medical advice. Consult a qualified herbalist or doctor for ongoing or serious symptoms.

Valerian potentiates sedative medications including benzodiazepines and barbiturates. Even as a bath, some systemic absorption is possible through the skin. Do not use this preparation if you take any sedative, sleeping tablet, or anti-anxiety medication. Do not combine with alcohol.

Do not drive or operate machinery on the same evening as a valerian bath if it is your first time using it, until you know how it affects you.

Consult a herbalist or your midwife before using this remedy in pregnancy.

Paediatric use is not adult-divided-by-half. Consult a herbalist who specialises in children's herbal medicine before using any herbal preparation in children under twelve.

content.text: Place 50 g of dried valerian root in a medium saucepan. Pour over one litre of cold water.
Bring to a gentle simmer, then remove from the heat. Cover the pan and steep for 20 minutes. The liquid will turn a pale amber-brown and smell strongly of valerian.
Strain the liquid through a sieve into a measuring jug, pressing the root to extract the liquid. Discard the spent herb.
Run a warm bath. Pour the strained valerian liquid into the bath water and stir to disperse.
Soak for 15-20 minutes. Pat dry and go to bed directly.
One bath per evening, taken 30-60 minutes before bed. Use for up to two weeks at a stretch. If tension or sleep problems persist beyond two weeks, consult a doctor.
Dried valerian root stores for up to 12 months in a sealed tin, kept in a cool dark place. Prepare the bath preparation fresh each time; do not store the liquid.
When not to use this remedy
Do not use this bath if you are on sedative medication, sleeping tablets, or anti-anxiety medication. Do not combine with alcohol on the same evening.
See a GP for insomnia lasting more than a month, insomnia with low mood. Loud snoring with daytime sleepiness, or any sudden change in sleep pattern in older adults.
